1) Neighborhood Reconstructing autoencoders (NRAEs) are a new graph-based regularization method that improves both overfit and connectivity of learned manifolds; 2) Compared to other graph-based methods, NRAE is simple and easy-to-implement; 3) Extensive experiments demonstrate that, in some cases, NRAE improves overfit and connectivity by significant margins.

1. A new Neighborhood Reconstructing autoencoder is proposed that simultaneously addresses overfitting and the local connectivity of the learned latent manifold; 2. Compared to existing autoencoders, the proposed method significantly reduces overfitting and improves the local connectivity of latent manifolds, in many cases by significant margins; and 3.

(1) neighborhood graph-based autoencoder regularization can simultaneously address overfitting and incorrect local connectivity in the latent space manifold; (2) neighborhood reconstruction loss is a simple and effective regularization loss that is easy to implement; (3) neighborhood reconstruction loss can be combined with existing regularization methods to improve performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
improving the quality of the manifold that autoencoders learn from data.

the following question: How can we design autoencoders that learn a better representation of data, one that is both more accurate in representing the training data, as well as more faithful to the local geometry of the data?
the following question: how do we learn a manifold that is both overfitting-free and has the correct local connectivity?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
NRAE is a simple and scalable method that improves upon existing methods in both the overfitting and the local connectivity of learned manifolds.

NRAE, which simultaneously addresses the issues of overfit and local connectivity, outperforms all the state-of-the-art autoencoders, including denoising, contractive, and graph-based ones, in terms of manifold reconstruction, manifold learning, and manifold interpolation.
NRAE is a simple and effective method for improving the quality of learned manifold.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, by merging local connectivity information and local quadratic approximations to the decoder function, NRAE simultaneously addresses overfitting and incorrect local connectivity, and is computationally efficient.
NRAE can be viewed as a graph-based regularization technique for vanilla autoencoders.
we propose a novel neighborhood reconstruction loss for autoencoders and demonstrate its effectiveness in improving overfitting and manifold connectivity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
neighborhood information, when properly incorporated, can be very effective in improving the quality of learned manifolds.
, by exploiting the neighborhood graph structure, one can improve the quality of learned manifolds by simultaneously mitigating overfitting and correcting the local connectivity.

, by exploiting the local quadratic approximation of the decoder function and the neighborhood reconstruction loss, we can obtain a simple yet effective regularization technique for vanilla autoencoders.
